newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban execute pregnant woman's strangler.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban execute pregnant woman's strangler.

text.p: The killer of a pregnant woman and her three children was executed on a Kabul high school playing field on Wednesday, shot with an assault rifle by the head of the family.
It was the capital's first public execution since the Islamic Taleban took control in September.
Ghulam Mohammed was shot on the soccer field at the Amani High School in central Kabul before an all-male crowd of about 3,000.
Ghulam Mohammed was taken to the school in a white pick-up truck flying the Taleban's trademark white flag, according to witnesses.
A Taleban cleric addressed the crowd from a loudspeaker truck before the execution took place. "He is being punished according to the law of Islam. Let this be a lesson for others," he said.
The school is next to the concrete traffic post where the Taleban hung the bodies of communist president Najibullah and his brother after killing them when they first took Kabul.

The executioner, Mohammed Alif, was handed a Kalashnikov assault rifle by a nearby Taleban militiaman. He dropped to one knee and fired a two-second burst of automatic fire at the condemned man from about 40 feet (10 metres).
He then walked over to the prostrate victim and fired another burst into his chest.
Under Islamic law, the family of a murder victim has the right to execute the murderer.
Ghulam Mohammed was convicted of strangling Mohammed Alif's wife, who neighbours said was eight months pregnant, and three small children during a burglary in December last year.
Ghulam Mohammed was convicted with two others -- one of them a 15-year-old girl -- of killing Mohammed Alif's family for $1,000.
He and another man were first convicted and sentenced to death under the ousted administration of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, but escaped from jail when the Taleban took Kabul.
The girl, who according to neighbours was trying to raise money to get married, was sentenced to three years in prison because of her age.
Ghulam Mohammed was subsequently recaptured, and, according to a Taleban official, his sentence was reconfirmed by the Taleban courts.
His two accomplices who escaped with him during the Taleban takeover of Kabul have not been recaptured.
Mohammed Alif told reporters after the execution: "I will not be happy until the last of the people involved is arrested."
Speaking at the execution, the Taleban cleric said: "In the past in Afghanistan there was no security. Now with the help of the Taleban movement, the rule of Islam has been established."
He said there were three elements to Islamic punishment: amputation, which is normally imposed for theft, stoning for adultery, and Qisas -- revenge killing -- as occurred on Wednesday.
The Taleban took over Kabul in late September and now control 75 per cent of the country. They have imposed their strict vision of Islamic law on the parts of the country they control.
